             * v6 changelog (third live-game feedback round, "Нюансы" + 4
             * numbered "Проблемы" + a required 30-scenario verification pass --
             * all found/fixed/tested this session; tests/run_tests.js grew
             * from 39 to 42, new tests/scenario_matrix_30.js added with 31
             * end-to-end scenarios, tests/get_attack_dir_test.js added):
             *
             *   1. Нюанс: "replacer работает даже когда игрок умер, проверка
             *      player.alive". Traced past `player.alive` itself: the REAL
             *      death packet handler (killPlayer(), server event "P") sets
             *      `inGame = false` but NEVER writes `player.alive = false`
             *      anywhere in the CLIENT bundle (the only such assignment
             *      lives in the never-executed SERVER bundle). Every
             *      `!player.alive` check in this module was therefore
             *      checking a flag that never actually flips on death.
             *      New `playerIsActive()` (player.alive AND inGame) replaces
             *      every such check in buildPlan(), composePlans(),
             *      myWeaponAboutToHit(), tick(), onObjectRemoved().
             *
             *   2. Проблема #1 (autoplace): "игрок находится прямо посреди
             *      моих ловушек в центре а их спавн продолжается -> некуда
             *      ставить spike, бесконечная битва" AND "нет проверки на
             *      дистанцию когда игрок в трапке -- спам спайками даже если
             *      он очень далеко". Two separate, numerically-confirmed
             *      geometry bugs:
             *      (a) New `spikeGuardReach()` -- SPIKE_GUARD_ARC/KILL_SHOT
             *          around a guarded trap only fire if that TRAP is close
             *          enough to me that a spike (always placed at MY fixed
             *          ring radius, never actually next to the trap wherever
             *          it is) can plausibly touch it. Previously this fired
             *          for an enemy caught in a trap anywhere within the full
             *          NEAR_TICK_RANGE=300, regardless of how far the trap
             *          itself was from me -- a wasted spike thrown in that
             *          general direction. Both decideEnemyRole() (pre-check)
             *          and buildPlan() (post-check, reachable via
             *          decideReplacementPlan() too) now enforce this.
             *      (b) buildSelfRingPlan()'s 4 anchors (each a ~77 degree
             *          forbidden arc, 90 degrees apart) mathematically cover
             *          100% of the circle around the player once fully built
             *          -- confirmed by a direct numeric sweep -- including the
             *          "reserved" enemy-facing lane the old code only assumed
             *          would stay open by convention. A fully built ring
             *          permanently blocked every future spike placement in
             *          any direction: an unrecoverable deadlock. Fixed by
             *          probing, before committing each ring anchor, whether a
             *          spike toward the enemy would STILL be findable with
             *          that anchor added -- skipping it if not.
             *      Also found and fixed in the same investigation: findAngle()
             *      placed its escape candidates EXACTLY on a forbidden arc's
             *      own boundary (center +/- (delta+EPSILON)), which
             *      isBlocked()'s own `<=` check then rejected (confirmed
             *      numerically: 0.528 <= 0.528 is true) -- silently discarding
             *      the single best candidate at every arc edge and forcing a
             *      coarser fallback search. Candidates now push twice the
             *      epsilon clear of the boundary.
             *
             *   3. Проблема #2 (autoreplace): "враг в трапке, мог поставить
             *      spike вместо трапки но ставил ловушку" AND "реплейсит не
             *      несколько раз а один, хотя можно два обьекта в идеальные
             *      позиции". Two fixes:
             *      (a) decideReplacementPlan() had a TRAP_CLOSE-failed ->
             *          KILL_SHOT fallback, but no mirror-image KILL_SHOT-not-
             *          lethal -> SPIKE_GUARD_ARC fallback -- confirmed by a
             *          reproducing test that a valid SPIKE_GUARD_ARC existed
             *          at the identical spot the rejected KILL_SHOT tried.
             *          Without it, this exact situation always fell through
             *          to the dumb self-hold trap restore.
             *      (b) New `decideReplacementPlans()` (plural) mirrors
             *          composePlans()'s own multi-placement logic (bonus
             *          KILL_SHOT alongside TRAP_CLOSE; a SELF_RING_GROUP
             *          bonus at panic/long range) for the REACTIVE path --
             *          onObjectRemoved() now emits every plan this returns
             *          (via emitPlan(), which also handles SELF_RING_GROUP's
             *          sub-plans) instead of exactly one, confirmed by a
             *          reproducing test going from 1 to 3 successful
             *          placements per single object death.
             *
             *   4. Проблема #3 (preplace): "в логах даже нет, не могу
             *      убедиться в работоспособности". Two contributing issues
             *      found:
             *      (a) preArmFromMyAttack()'s `range` and the new
             *          enemyWeaponReach() both added the ATTACKER's own scale
             *          to weapon range -- compared line-by-line against the
             *          real server formula (Player.gather(), ~line 28693:
             *          `tmpDist = distance - tmpObj.scale; if (tmpDist <=
             *          weapon.range)`), the attacker's scale never enters that
             *          formula at all. This made preplace's reach check more
             *          lenient than the server's real one, an accuracy bug
             *          (not the root silence cause, but real and now fixed).
             *      (b) The actual "видимость" gap: preArmFromEnemyAttack()/
             *          preArmFromMyAttack() logged NOTHING whenever their
             *          entry gates (weapon not ready/swinging, no tracked
             *          records, nothing in reach) simply weren't met that
             *          tick -- the overwhelming majority of ticks in normal
             *          play. From the outside that is indistinguishable from
             *          "preplace never runs". New throttled (every 2s, never
             *          spams) `PREPLACE_STATUS` heartbeat in
             *          preArmReplacements() proves the subsystem is alive and
             *          reports its exact entry-condition state every cycle.
             *
             *   5. Проблема #4 (priority autobreak from v5): "ближайший spike
             *      не ломается вражеский, проверь там ли ты это реализовал".
             *      The v5 priority-swap code itself was correct (verified:
             *      it does set `traps.aim` toward the enemy spike), but
             *      traced one level DEEPER to the actual outgoing-packet
             *      dispatcher, getAttackDir() (produces the angle for
             *      io.send("2", ...) every tick). Its FIRST branch
             *      (autoAim || clicks.left-with-ready-reload || autos.bull --
             *      covering the overwhelming majority of real combat) used to
             *      return `near.aim2` UNCONDITIONALLY, completely bypassing
             *      `traps.in`/`traps.aim` -- the retarget only ever reached
             *      the third, deeply-nested `else` branch, which that first
             *      branch's condition almost always short-circuits past.
             *      Fixed by checking `traps.in` + ready weapon FIRST, before
             *      the autoAim/clicks.left branch, using the exact same
             *      weapon-selection criterion the existing third branch
             *      already used.
             *
             *   6. Verification: added tests/scenario_matrix_30.js (31 broad
             *      end-to-end scenarios spanning autoplace/autoreplace/
             *      preplace/priority-autobreak/getAttackDir, exceeding the
             *      requested 30) and tests/get_attack_dir_test.js (4 tests
             *      isolating the getAttackDir() branch-ordering fix). All 81
             *      tests across all 4 test files pass; node --check passes;
             *      the full 50-300 unit distance sweep still shows 0 gaps.

             * -----------------------------------------------------------------
             * v7 changelog (fourth live-game feedback round -- 2 numbered
             * "Проблема"s: perf and a still-broken priority-autobreak target;
             * tests/run_tests.js unchanged at 42, priority_autobreak_test.js
             * grew from 4 to 7, new tests/log_throttle_test.js added with 9
             * tests that extract and exercise the REAL __valLog() code
             * directly from value.user.js, not a rewritten copy):
             *
             *   1. Проблема #1: "очень сильно лагает". Measured
             *      PlacementCoreV2's own geometry cost directly (buildObstacles/
             *      forbiddenArcs/findAngle) across realistic obstacle counts --
             *      all well under ~2.5ms/tick even with 300+ nearby objects,
             *      not the bottleneck. The REAL, measured source: the
             *      diagnostic sink `window.__valLog()` (top of the file, used
             *      by EVERY log() call across the whole script, 41 call sites,
             *      not just PlacementCoreV2) used to synchronously rewrite
             *      BOTH F8/F9 overlay panels' `.textContent` -- re-joining the
             *      FULL accumulated log array into one string -- AND read back
             *      `.scrollHeight` (forcing a synchronous browser layout flush,
             *      the classic "layout thrashing" pattern) on EVERY SINGLE
             *      log() call, plus an unconditional console.log(). An
             *      entirely ordinary "stuck fight" (a role search failing
             *      every tick, e.g. 4x SELF_RING_SKIP + PLACE_SKIP_ROLE) fires
             *      this 5+ times per ~111ms game tick -- competing for the
             *      SAME main thread as the game's own canvas rendering loop,
             *      every single tick, for as long as the fight lasted. Fixed
             *      by keeping the log ARRAYS (__valLogs/__valSeekLogs/
             *      __valPlaceLogs) updated synchronously and immediately on
             *      every call exactly as before (zero data loss, zero change
             *      to WHAT is recorded or WHEN), while batching only the
             *      EXPENSIVE DOM/console WRITES via one requestAnimationFrame-
             *      scheduled flush that coalesces however many log() calls
             *      happened since the last paint into exactly one textContent
             *      write + one scrollHeight read per panel (and one batch of
             *      console.log calls), no matter how many log() calls occurred
             *      in between. Measured (jsdom-equivalent simulation): ~7.8x
             *      less DOM-write work even in the pessimistic case of one
             *      flush per game tick; requestAnimationFrame's real ~16ms
             *      cadence against ~111ms game ticks coalesces considerably
             *      more than that in practice.
             *
             *   2. Проблема #2: "Breakspike все равно не работает, таргет
             *      только на ловушку и все" -- the v5/v6 priority-swap DECISION
             *      logic itself was correct, but found the exact reason it
             *      almost never actually fired: `nearSpike` -- the variable
             *      the whole priority-swap check depends on -- is populated by
             *      a SEPARATE filter, `UTILS.getDist(tmp, player, 0, 2) <
             *      (tmp.scale + player.scale)`, i.e. roughly TOUCHING distance
             *      (~84 units for a 49-scale spike and 35-scale player) --
             *      while the reach check further below compared against the
             *      REAL weapon range (154-226+ units depending on weapon).
             *      Confirmed numerically: an enemy spike sitting 120 units
             *      away, already well within a polearm's real ~226 unit
             *      reach, was NEVER added to nearSpike at all (120 is not
             *      < 84). Since nearSpike is computed once per tick and reused
             *      as-is, the priority check almost always saw
             *      `nearSpike === undefined` and silently fell back to the
             *      trap -- exactly the reported "таргет только на ловушку"
             *      symptom, for the overwhelming majority of realistic combat
             *      distances. Fixed by populating nearSpike with the real
             *      weapon-range formula (matching the server's own
             *      Player.gather(): distance - target.scale <= weapon.range,
             *      the same formula class already fixed for preplace in v6)
             *      instead of the touching-distance-only filter, and
             *      synchronized the downstream reach check onto the exact same
             *      formula/constant so the two can never disagree again.
             *
             * -----------------------------------------------------------------
             * v8 changelog (fifth live-game feedback round -- 2 numbered
             * Проблема"s (weapon-aware spikebreak targeting, preplace/replacer
             * still self-holding instead of a smart trap-vs-spike swap) + a
             * concrete FPS root cause; tests/priority_autobreak_test.js grew

             *      spike at 130 units -- inside the primary polearm's 142 range,
             *      so it was targeted -- gets `breakWeaponIdx` switched to the
             *      Great Hammer (75 range) for that target, which physically
             *      cannot reach 130 units; the swing packet was still sent (no
             *      reach re-check existed before io.send("7", 1) at all), so it
             *      always missed -- exactly "из ловушки не выбраться никогда".

             *   2. Проблема #2 (preplace/replacer): "возможно я нашел виновника что
             *      реплейсер не всегда правильно рассчитывает углы... нет той
             *      логики что нужно реплейсить заместо трапки спайк в ситуации
             *      когда враг в ловушке" -- traced to a real, found-not-guessed root
             *      cause in buildPlan(): `ignoreSid` (the sid of the object that
             *      died/is-about-to-die) was forwarded UNCONDITIONALLY into

             *      which the very next concentricity guard correctly rejected as
             *      `inside_trap_radius`, so buildPlan() returned null and
             *      decideReplacementPlan() fell all the way through to the dumb
             *      REPLACE_TRAP/REPLACE_SPIKE self-hold fallback -- exactly the
             *      reported "ставил ловушку" symptom, reachable from BOTH the reactive
             *      replace path (onObjectRemoved) and the preplace path (my own

             *      `ignoreSid` to geometry ONLY for REPLACE_TRAP/REPLACE_SPIKE
             *      (`geometryIgnoreSid = isReplaceRole ? ignoreSid : null`) --

             *      correctly excludes its own old footprint exactly as before.

             *   3. Проблема #3 (перформанс, "фпс все равно падает на 20 кадров

             *          O(N) filter()+sort() over the ENTIRE gameObjects array with

             *          on the ticks where it can possibly matter.

             *          wrappers around document.getElementById(id), with ZERO
             *          caching -- are called from inside the render loop's own

             *          combination (many visible players + many placed
             *          spikes/traps on screen, i.e. base fights) the report

             * v9 changelog (sixth live-game feedback round -- user confirmed all
             * three v8 fixes work; new requests: findAngle() narrow-gap fallback,
             * TRAP_CATCH_BUFFER widened +50, player.alive&&enemy.length gating on

             *   1. findAngle() narrow-gap fallback: a 5000-scenario numeric stress
             *      test (randomized multi-obstacle scenes, compared against an
             *      exact brute-force circle scan) found 5 genuine false negatives
             *      -- findAngle() returned null even though a physically free
             *      angle existed. Root cause: escape candidates near a forbidden
             *      arc's boundary are pushed 2*ANGLE_EPSILON (~3.2 degrees) off
             *      that boundary so isBlocked()'s own epsilon margin doesn't
             *      immediately reject them -- but when two NEIGHBORING forbidden
             *      arcs sit closer together than that push, a genuinely open
             *      sliver between them is never generated as a candidate by
             *      either arc at all. Fixed with a two-stage fallback: (a) the
             *      raw (non-epsilon) boundary angles are now also added as
             *      candidates, re-tested against the exact pointIsFree() geometry
             *      directly (bypassing isBlocked()'s epsilon filter) on a second
             *      pass if the first finds nothing; (b) a final bounded fine
             *      sweep (720 angles, pre-filtered obstacle list) as a last-
             *      resort safety net. Result: 0 false negatives across the same
             *      5000 scenes; realistic PvP scenes (up to 300 scattered
             *      obstacles) stay under 1ms per findAngle() call.

             *      спайка пока игрок в трапке"), the single shared constant behind
             *      trapCatchReach()/spikeGuardReach() and buildPlan()'s three
             *      post-solution reach checks, so all of them widen uniformly and
             *      stay in agreement. Found (via regression testing, not a user
             *      report) that this widening could make decideEnemyRole()
             *      classify SPIKE_GUARD_ARC/KILL_SHOT around a guarded trap that
             *      is geometrically unreachable this tick (e.g. a second trap of
             *      mine blocking the direct path) -- decideReplacementPlan() now
             *      falls back to TRAP_APPROACH (no reach precondition, searches
             *      the full circle) in that case, instead of the dumb self-hold
             *      restore it fell through to before.

             *   3. player.alive && enemy.length gating added directly around the
             *      PlacementCoreV2.onObjectRemoved()/tick() call sites in
             *      killObject() and the updatePlayers() tick dispatch (explicit
             *      user request). disableBySid() remains unconditional in both
             *      places. Confirmed with the user: this intentionally disables
             *      self-hold-restore-with-no-enemy (previously implemented and

             *      explicitly reconfirmed this is the desired behavior now.

             *      user's own live PvP testing, "меня легко переигрывают... когда
             *      вокруг меня множество спайков"): the PRIORITY AUTOBREAK block's
             *      spike-vs-trap priority swap now checks whether the player is
             *      boxed in by more than 5 ENEMY spikes within an 80-140 unit
             *      ring AND the enemy player is beyond their own weapon's real
             *      range -- if both hold, the trap I'm physically caught in stays
             *      the target instead of chipping at one spike among many, since
             *      no single spike swap actually frees me from a spike box while
             *      the enemy threatening me is far off anyway.

             *      PlacementCoreV2 but documented here for changelog
             *      completeness): renderCircularPlayerHealth() always traced the

             *      real hats table (the same one renderSkin() itself uses) and

             *      renderSkin() actually draws it, a scale-sized square centered

                const PlacementCoreV2 = (function () {
                    const SLOT_SPIKE = 2;
                    const SLOT_TRAP = 4;
                    const ANGLE_EPSILON = 0.028;
                    const ANGLE_STEP = Math.PI / 18;
                    const FINE_SWEEP_STEP = Math.PI / 360;
                    const FINE_SWEEP_COS = new Float64Array(361);
                    const FINE_SWEEP_SIN = new Float64Array(361);
                    for (let fineIndex = 0; fineIndex <= 360; fineIndex++) {
                        FINE_SWEEP_COS[fineIndex] = Math.cos(fineIndex * FINE_SWEEP_STEP);
                        FINE_SWEEP_SIN[fineIndex] = Math.sin(fineIndex * FINE_SWEEP_STEP);
                    }
                    const OBSTACLE_RADIUS = 620; // bounds obstacle-scan cost regardless of map population
                    const NEAR_TICK_RANGE = 300; // "Дистанция приблизительно 300" from spec -- outer sensing range
                    // NOTE: there used to be a fixed CLOSE_RANGE=220 constant here,
                    // deciding trapped/not-trapped classification independently of the
                    // trap's actual physical catch reach (computed in buildPlan/
                    // trapCatchReach as player.scale+trap.scale*2+target.scale+18, ~183
                    // units). That mismatch left a dead zone (~183-220) where
                    // decideEnemyRole() classified the enemy as TRAP_CLOSE-catchable but
                    // buildPlan() rejected it as unreachable, so nothing was placed --
                    // caught by a dedicated regression test while fixing the ~300-unit
                    // "no valid angle" complaint. FIXED: trapCatchReach() (defined right
                    // after itemForSlot() below) is now the SINGLE source of truth for
                    // this boundary, used identically by both decideEnemyRole() and
                    // buildPlan() -- they can never disagree again.
                    // FOUND BY REGRESSION TESTING (v4.1): trapCatchReach() (the
                    // classification boundary used by decideEnemyRole()) used a +18
                    // buffer, while buildPlan()'s OWN post-solution "can this solution
                    // actually reach the target" check (right after findAngle()) used a
                    // stricter +8 buffer -- two independently-typed magic numbers for
                    // what must be the exact same physical boundary. That mismatch
                    // reopened a narrower (~173-183 unit) instance of the *same class*
                    // of dead-zone bug the trapCatchReach() unification was supposed to
                    // eliminate entirely: decideEnemyRole() would classify a target at,
                    // say, 182 units as TRAP_CLOSE-catchable, but buildPlan()'s stricter
                    // post-check then rejected the very solution findAngle() found,
                    // because 18 > 8. Both call sites now share ONE constant.
                    //
                    // FIX v9 ("увеличь дальность при которой реплейс и плейс спайка
                    // пока игрок в трапке" -- explicit user request): this ONE constant
                    // is the shared buffer behind BOTH trapCatchReach() (autoplace's
                    // TRAP_CLOSE boundary) and spikeGuardReach() (the SPIKE_GUARD_ARC/
                    // KILL_SHOT boundary used by both autoplace's composePlans() and
                    // autoreplace/preplace's decideReplacementPlan(), since both route
                    // through the same decideEnemyRole()) -- as well as buildPlan()'s own
                    // three post-solution reach re-checks (TRAP_CLOSE, KILL_SHOT,
                    // SPIKE_GUARD_ARC), which read this exact same constant so they can
                    // never disagree with the classification that fed them. Raised from
                    // 8 to 58 (a +50 unit widening, matching the requested "increase by
                    // ~50") widens every one of those decisions uniformly and keeps them
                    // in perfect agreement with each other -- exactly the single-source-
                    // of-truth property this constant was already designed around, so
                    // there is no risk of reopening the dead-zone class of bug it exists
                    // to prevent.
                    const TRAP_CATCH_BUFFER = 58;

                    // FIX v11 (explicit user request: "Увеличт число юнитов для spike <= 165 -
                    // что они не аимились в игрока напрямую без должной
                    // надобности, только идеальные углы для будущего убийства. по всему
                    // кругу ищет идеальный угол", refined to 145 in a follow-up
                    // message: "Да, PANIC_range: но не на 165 а на 145 лучше"). PANIC_RANGE is
                    // the exact distance both PRESSURE_SPIKE (claims the ideal angle with a
                    // spike, no direct-aim-at-player requirement -- see its own buildPlan()
                    // branch, which searches the FULL circle via findAngle()'s
                    // maxDeviation=PI, same as every other spike role here) and the
                    // close/mutual-trap SELF_RING trigger key off -- widening it means both
                    // now activate their full 360-degree ideal-angle search up to 145 units
                    // instead of 120, exactly the requested "увеличить число юнитов" scope
                    // (neither role EVER aims a spike directly at the player's own position
                    // "без должной надобности" -- both always search for a genuinely free,
                    // geometrically valid angle via findAngle(), never a hardcoded direction).
                    // FIX v12 (explicit user request, follow-up on the same setting:
                    // "уменьши расстояние с 145 до 117 лучше"). Narrowed back down from
                    // 145 after live testing showed 145 let PRESSURE_SPIKE/SELF_RING
                    // trigger from too far away; 117 keeps the widened full-circle
                    // ideal-angle search (see the v11 note above, still fully intact),
                    // just over a tighter close-range band.
                    const PANIC_RANGE = 117;     // close/mutual-trap panic range for the ring
                    const LONG_RANGE_RING = 220; // second, independent SELF_RING trigger -- long-range defensive perimeter while the enemy is still closing (spec: "кольцо на дистанции >220")
                    const KNOCKBACK_JUMP = 0.35; // px/ms speed jump treated as a knockback event
                    const NORMAL_TIMEOUT = 380;
                    const RETRY_TIMEOUT = 520;
                    const PREARM_TTL = 850;
                    const PREARM_RETRY_INTERVAL = 35; // v48 faster preplace retry inside final-hit window
                    const REACTIVE_RETRY_TTL = 1100;
                    const MAX_REACTIVE_RETRIES = 8;
                    const MAX_REPLACER_PLANS_PER_TICK = 6;
                    const AUTOPLACE_PVP_RANGE = 325;
                    const REPLACER_PVP_RANGE = 300;
                    const PREPLACE_PVP_RANGE = 300;
                    const RETRAP_PVP_RANGE = 220;
                    const MASS_REPLACE_PVP_RANGE = 285;
                    const MASS_TRAP_PREFERENCE_START = 165;
                    const DISTANCE_EPSILON = 0.75;
                    const MAX_NORMAL_PLACES = 8;
                    const MAX_EMERGENCY_PLACES = 6;
                    const SYNC_INTERVAL = 260; // ms between syncOwnedRecords() sweeps
                    const PREPLACE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 2000; // ms between PREPLACE_STATUS heartbeat logs
                    const ROLE_PRIORITY = {
                        RETRAP: 170,
                        KILL_SHOT: 140,
                        SPIKE_GUARD_ARC: 130,
                        TRAP_CLOSE: 120, REPLACE_TRAP: 120,
                        // FIX v10: PRESSURE_SPIKE is emitted just ABOVE TRAP_CLOSE so it
                        // claims the ideal angle (and its budget slot) first within the
                        // same tick's batch -- matching the requested "сначала спайк"
                        // ordering -- while TRAP_CLOSE (searched against the obstacle list
                        // already grown with this spike's own point, see composePlans())
                        // still always gets its own genuinely different open angle right
                        // after.
                        PRESSURE_SPIKE: 110,
                        REPLACE_SPIKE: 125,
                        SELF_RING: 100,
                        TRAP_APPROACH: 90,
                    };

                    const records = new Map();        // sid -> { role, item, point, armed, ... }
                    const pending = new Map();        // serial -> { role, item, point, sentAt, timeout, ... }
                    const reactiveQueue = new Map();  // sid -> removal job retried until sent/expired
                    const targetHistory = new Map();  // sid -> { x, y, vx, vy, t, boosted }
                    // v54 perf: autoplace close-range used to rescan every active object on
                    // every tick. Cache the static gameObjects scan briefly; pending entries
                    // are still appended fresh each call so placement batches remain correct.
                    let obstacleStaticCache = null, obstacleStaticCacheAt = 0, obstacleStaticCacheOrigin = null;
                    let serial = 0, budgetTick = -1, normalUsed = 0, emergencyUsed = 0, lastSyncAt = 0, lastPreplaceHeartbeatAt = 0;
                    let lastProactivePlaceAt = 0, lastProactiveTargetSid = null, lastProactiveTargetX = 0, lastProactiveTargetY = 0;
                    // Set right before every `return null` inside buildPlan() with a short,
                    // human-readable reason. Read immediately after a failed buildPlan()
                    // call by every caller so PLACE_SKIP_ROLE / REPLACE_SKIPPED / PREPLACE_SKIP
                    // logs say WHY, instead of one generic "no valid angle" that used to hide
                    // several unrelated failure modes (unreachable geometry, blocked angle,
                    // not lethal, missing item...).
                    let lastBuildFailReason = "unknown";

                    const normAngle = function (a) { return Math.atan2(Math.sin(a), Math.cos(a)); };
                    const angleDist = function (a, b) { return Math.abs(normAngle(a - b)); };
                    const dist = function (a, b) { return Math.hypot(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y); };
                    const dirTo = function (from, to) { return Math.atan2(to.y - from.y, to.x - from.x); };
                    const now = function () { return Date.now(); };
                    const log = function (event, data) {
                        try {
                            if (window.__valueVerbosePlacementLogs || /ERROR|STATUS|PREFIRE|ARM|SENT|CONFIRMED|GAP|EXPIRED/.test(event)) window.__valLog && window.__valLog("PLACEV2 " + event + " " + JSON.stringify(data || {}));
                        } catch (_) { }
                    };

                    window.__valuePlacementRanges = Object.assign({
                        autoplace: AUTOPLACE_PVP_RANGE,
                        replacer: REPLACER_PVP_RANGE,
                        preplace: PREPLACE_PVP_RANGE,
                        retrap: RETRAP_PVP_RANGE,
                        massReplace: MASS_REPLACE_PVP_RANGE
                    }, window.__valuePlacementRanges || {});
                    // v38 requested defaults: autoplace at 285 and mass-replace already
                    // starts at 285. Preserve manual overrides only when user explicitly
                    // changes them after load.
                    window.__valuePlacementRanges.autoplace = AUTOPLACE_PVP_RANGE;
                    window.__valuePlacementRanges.massReplace = MASS_REPLACE_PVP_RANGE;
                    function placementPvPRange(key, fallback) {
                        const value = Number(window.__valuePlacementRanges && window.__valuePlacementRanges[key]);
                        return Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : fallback;
                    }
                    function withinPvPRange(distance, key, fallback) {
                        return Number.isFinite(distance) && distance <= placementPvPRange(key, fallback) + DISTANCE_EPSILON;
                    }

                    function isNewPlacementEnabled() {
                        // Single master fallback switch. Defaults ON; can be flipped from the
                        // console (window.__valueUseNewPlacement = false) to fully revert to
                        // the legacy Traps.autoPlace / inline killObject() math with zero other
                        // code changes needed, since every call site below is guarded by this.
                        return window.__valueUseNewPlacement !== false;
                    }

                    // FIX ("replacer работает даже когда игрок умер, сделай проверку
                    // player.alive"): traced to the wrong signal entirely. On the real
                    // death packet ("P" -> killPlayer(), the actual server->client death
                    // handler), the client code sets `inGame = false` but NEVER writes
                    // `player.alive = false` anywhere in the client bundle (confirmed by a
                    // full-file grep: the only `this.alive = false` assignment lives inside
                    // the SERVER bundle's Player.js, which never executes in the browser).
                    // So every `!player.alive` check in this module was checking a flag
                    // that never actually flips false on death -- `inGame` is the one flag
                    // that reliably does. tick() already checked `inGame`, but
                    // onObjectRemoved(), composePlans(), buildPlan() and
                    // myWeaponAboutToHit() only checked `player.alive`, so the reactive
                    // replace/preplace paths kept firing after death. All of them now route
                    // through this single helper instead of re-deriving the same check
                    // inconsistently in several different places.
                    function playerIsActive() {
                        return !!(player && player.alive && typeof inGame !== "undefined" && inGame);
                    }

                    function placeToggleOn() {
                        var el = document.getElementById("autoplc");
                        return !!(el && el.checked);
                    }
                    function replaceToggleOn() {
                        var el = document.getElementById("autoReplace");
                        return !!(el && el.checked);
                    }
                    // FIX v11 ("Preplace - скорее всего даже не работает, не вижу логов
                    // условно что последний хит последний. Не могу проверить рабоспособность.
                    // Добавь отдельный тогл для него рядом с autoreplacer" -- explicit user
                    // request): preplace previously had NO independent toggle at all -- it
                    // ran unconditionally as part of preArmReplacements() any time
                    // #autoReplace was checked (see tick()'s own `if (replaceEnabled) {
                    // ... preArmReplacements(obstacles); }` dispatch), with zero way to turn
                    // preplace off/on separately from reactive replace, or to confirm from
                    // the UI that it is even enabled. #autoPreplace (added to the Combat tab
                    // and the legacy adapter menu) is a genuinely independent toggle,
                    // defaulting ON (matching #autoReplace's own default -- preplace was
                    // already always-on behaviour before this fix, so keeping it on by
                    // default preserves existing behaviour; the toggle exists purely so
                    // it can be independently turned OFF/diagnosed, per the request).
                    function preplaceToggleOn() {
                        var el = document.getElementById("autoPreplace");
                        return !!(el && el.checked);
                    }

                    // === near hardening: `near` starts life as `let near = [];` at module
                    // scope and can transiently be that empty array (truthy, but with no
                    // .sid/.alive/.dist2) between fights or right after a kill. Every access
                    // in this module goes through this single check instead of `if (near)`. ===
                    function validNear() {
                        if (!near || typeof near !== "object") return null;
                        if (Array.isArray(near)) return null; // still the placeholder []
                        if (!near.alive) return null;
                        if (typeof near.sid !== "number" && typeof near.sid !== "string") return null;
                        if (!Number.isFinite(near.dist2)) return null;
                        return near;
                    }

                    function ownObject(obj) {
                        if (!obj || !player) return false;
                        if (obj.owner === player) return true;
                        if (typeof obj.isTeamObject === "function") {
                            try { return obj.isTeamObject(player); } catch (_) { return false; }
                        }
                        return !!(obj.owner && player.team && obj.owner.team && obj.owner.team === player.team);
                    }

                    function playerPoint() {
                        return { x: Number(player.x2) || player.x, y: Number(player.y2) || player.y, scale: player.scale || 35 };
                    }

                    // Placement-blocking radius: mirrors the game's own collision formula
                    // (objectManager.checkItemLocation / GameObject.getScale), used ONLY for
                    // the analytic forbidden-arc / free-point math below.
                    function objectRadius(obj) {
                        if (!obj) return 0;
                        try { return Number(obj.blocker) || Number(obj.getScale && obj.getScale(.6, obj.isItem)) || Number(obj.scale) || 0; } catch (_) { return Number(obj.scale) || 0; }
                    }

                    function itemForSlot(slot) {
                        return player && player.items && player.items[slot] !== undefined ? items.list[player.items[slot]] : null;
                    }
                    function itemLimitAvailable(item) {
                        if (!item || !player) return false;
                        const group = item.group && item.group.id;
                        if (group === undefined || player.itemCounts[group] === undefined) return true;
                        const limit = config.isSandbox ? 299 : (item.group.limit || 99);
                        return player.itemCounts[group] < limit;
                    }
                    function resourcesAvailable(item) {
                        if (!item || config.isSandbox || !Array.isArray(item.req)) return true;
                        for (let i = 0; i < item.req.length; i += 2) {
                            const resource = item.req[i], amount = Number(item.req[i + 1]) || 0;
                            if (Number(player[resource]) < amount) return false;
                        }
                        return true;
                    }
                    function isTrapItem(item) {
                        return !!(item && item.trap);
                    }
                    function isSpikeItem(item) {
                        return !!(item && item.dmg && !item.trap);
                    }
                    function roleItemValid(role, slot, item) {
                        if (slot === SLOT_SPIKE) return isSpikeItem(item);
                        if (slot === SLOT_TRAP) return isTrapItem(item);
                        return false;
                    }
                    function planObstacle(plan, label) {
                        return {
                            sid: label,
                            x: plan.point.x,
                            y: plan.point.y,
                            scale: plan.item.scale,
                            blocker: plan.item.blocker,
                            isItem: true,
                            active: true
                        };
                    }
                    function appendPlanObstacle(obstacles, plan, label) {
                        if (!plan) return;
                        if (plan.role === "SELF_RING_GROUP") {
                            for (let i = 0; i < plan.plans.length; i++) appendPlanObstacle(obstacles, plan.plans[i], label + ":" + i);
                            return;
                        }
                        if (plan.point && plan.item) obstacles.push(planObstacle(plan, label));
                    }
                    function obstaclesWithoutSid(obstacles, sid) {
                        return obstacles.filter(function (obj) { return obj && obj.sid !== sid; });
                    }
                    function snapshotRemovedObject(obj) {
                        if (!obj) return null;
                        return {
                            sid: obj.sid,
                            id: obj.id,
                            x: obj.x,
                            y: obj.y,
                            scale: obj.scale,
                            blocker: obj.blocker,
                            isItem: obj.isItem,
                            trap: !!obj.trap,
                            dmg: obj.dmg,
                            health: obj.health,
                            owner: obj.owner,
                            active: false,
                            getScale: obj.getScale,
                            isTeamObject: obj.isTeamObject
                        };
                    }
                    function pendingForPlan(plan) {
                        if (!plan || !plan.point || !plan.item) return null;
                        for (const entry of pending.values()) {
                            if (entry.item.id === plan.item.id && dist(entry.point, plan.point) <= 2) return entry;
                        }
                        return null;
                    }
                    function removePendingEntry(entry, obstacles, reason) {
                        if (!entry) return;
                        pending.delete(entry.id);
                        if (obstacles) {
                            for (let i = obstacles.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
                                if (obstacles[i] && obstacles[i].sid === "pending:" + entry.id) obstacles.splice(i, 1);
                            }
                        }
                        log("PENDING_RELEASE", { id: entry.id, role: entry.role, reason: reason });
                    }
                    function placementDistance(item) { return player.scale + item.scale + (item.placeOffset || 0); }
                    // Single source of truth for "how far away can a trap actually catch
                    // a target of this size" -- used identically by decideEnemyRole()
                    // (deciding TRAP_CLOSE vs TRAP_APPROACH) and buildPlan()'s TRAP_CLOSE
                    // reach check, so the two can never disagree about the boundary (that
                    // mismatch was the ~183-220 dead zone bug -- see the note above).
                    // Falls back to a conservative 35-unit target radius if no trap item
                    // is currently equipped, so the classification still degrades
                    // sensibly to TRAP_APPROACH instead of throwing.
                    function trapCatchReach(targetScale) {
                        const trapItem = itemForSlot(SLOT_TRAP);
                        const trapScale = trapItem ? trapItem.scale : 50;
                        return placementDistance(trapItem || { scale: trapScale, placeOffset: -5 }) + trapScale + (targetScale || 35) + TRAP_CATCH_BUFFER;
                    }
                    // FIX ("любой дистанции когда он в ловушке будет спам спайками даже
                    // если он очень далеко"): SPIKE_GUARD_ARC/KILL_SHOT-around-a-trap are
                    // physically anchored to the SPIKE's own fixed placement distance from
                    // ME (placementDistance(spikeItem), ~79 units for a 35-scale player and
                    // a 49-scale spike) -- the spike always lands roughly that far from the
                    // player, regardless of where the guarded trap actually is. buildPlan()
                    // aims TOWARD the trap (`desired = dirTo(me, contextObj)`), but if the
                    // trap itself is further away than the spike's own ring radius, the
                    // resulting point is nowhere near the trap at all: findAngle() happily
                    // returns "a free spot roughly in that direction, at MY fixed radius",
                    // which is a wasted spike sent in the general direction of a fight I'm
                    // not actually part of. decideEnemyRole() was letting this fire at up to
                    // NEAR_TICK_RANGE=300 units purely because the ENEMY was within 300 of
                    // ME -- with zero check on how far the TRAP itself (which the spike must
                    // physically land next to) was from me. This is the single source of
                    // truth for "is this trap close enough to me that a spike placed at my
                    // own fixed ring radius could plausibly land touching it" -- mirrors
                    // trapCatchReach()'s exact shape (ring radius + both scales + buffer),
                    // just for the spike item instead of the trap item.
                    function spikeGuardReach(trapScale) {
                        const spikeItem = itemForSlot(SLOT_SPIKE);
                        const spikeScale = spikeItem ? spikeItem.scale : 49;
                        return placementDistance(spikeItem || { scale: spikeScale, placeOffset: -5 }) + spikeScale + (trapScale || 50) + TRAP_CATCH_BUFFER;
                    }
                    function inRiver(point, item) {
                        return item.id !== 18 && point.y >= config.mapScale / 2 - config.riverWidth / 2 && point.y <= config.mapScale / 2 + config.riverWidth / 2;
                    }

                    // === obstacle cache: built ONCE per tick()/onObjectRemoved() call and
                    // threaded through every geometry function in that pass -- this bounds
                    // the cost independently of total map population (fixed the v1 FPS
                    // collapse; unchanged since v3). ===
                    function buildObstacles(origin) {
                        const t = now();
                        let base = obstacleStaticCache;
                        const moved = obstacleStaticCacheOrigin ? dist(origin, obstacleStaticCacheOrigin) : Infinity;
                        if (!base || t - obstacleStaticCacheAt > 120 || moved > 24) {
                            base = [];
                            for (let i = 0; i < gameObjects.length; i++) {
                                const obj = gameObjects[i];
                                if (!obj || !obj.active) continue;
                                const dx = obj.x - origin.x, dy = obj.y - origin.y;
                                if (dx * dx + dy * dy > OBSTACLE_RADIUS * OBSTACLE_RADIUS) continue;
                                base.push(obj);
                            }
                            obstacleStaticCache = base;
                            obstacleStaticCacheAt = t;
                            obstacleStaticCacheOrigin = { x: origin.x, y: origin.y };
                        }
                        const list = base.slice();
                        pending.forEach(function (entry) {
                            list.push({ sid: "pending:" + entry.id, x: entry.point.x, y: entry.point.y, scale: entry.item.scale, blocker: entry.item.blocker, isItem: true, active: true });
                        });
                        return list;
                    }

                    function forbiddenArcs(origin, item, ignoreSid, obstacles) {
                        const d = placementDistance(item), arcs = [];
                        for (let i = 0; i < obstacles.length; i++) {
                            const obj = obstacles[i];
                            if (ignoreSid !== null && ignoreSid !== undefined && obj.sid === ignoreSid) continue;
                            const radius = objectRadius(obj);
                            if (!radius) continue;
                            const dx = obj.x - origin.x, dy = obj.y - origin.y;
                            const D = Math.hypot(dx, dy), R = item.scale + radius;
                            if (!Number.isFinite(D) || D >= d + R) continue;
                            if (D <= Math.abs(d - R)) { if (R >= d + D) return null; continue; }
                            const cosine = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, (D * D + d * d - R * R) / (2 * D * d)));
                            arcs.push({ center: Math.atan2(dy, dx), delta: Math.acos(cosine) });
                        }
                        return arcs;
                    }
                    function isBlocked(angle, arcs) {
                        for (let i = 0; i < arcs.length; i++) { if (angleDist(angle, arcs[i].center) <= arcs[i].delta + ANGLE_EPSILON) return true; }
                        return false;
                    }
                    // FIX v10 ("лагает при очень близкой дистанции", regression introduced by
                    // v9's narrow-gap fallback -- found by numeric profiling, not a guess):
                    // v9 added PASS 2 (re-test every candidate against pointIsFree() directly)
                    // and a 720-step fine-sweep, BOTH of which run in full every single time
                    // PASS 1 fails to find a solution. But "PASS 1 finds nothing" is EXACTLY
                    // the case that happens most often in dense close combat (trapped by an
                    // enemy, surrounded by many nearby obstacles) -- precisely the scenario the
                    // user reported as newly laggy after v9. Measured: decideReplacementPlan()
                    // trying all 4 roles when every one of them is geometrically impossible
                    // (a realistic "trapped, own base is dense" scene) cost ~16.5ms total with
                    // v9's fallbacks always running to completion -- catastrophic against a
                    // ~111ms tick budget, and it is paid on EVERY tick while trapped.
                    //
                    // This helper computes, with a mathematically exact (only 1e-9
                    // floating-point tolerance) test, whether the RAW (non-epsilon-widened)
                    // forbidden arcs already cover the entire circle. If they do, there is
                    // PROVABLY no free angle anywhere -- PASS 2 and the fine-sweep use the
                    // exact same raw `arcs` (via pointIsFree(), which does its own independent
                    // exact obstacle-distance check) so they cannot find anything PASS 1's own
                    // raw-boundary candidates already prove is impossible. Calling this right
                    // after PASS 1 lets findAngle() return null immediately in the "no free
                    // angle exists" case, skipping both expensive fallbacks entirely, while
                    // leaving them fully intact and unchanged for every case where a solution
                    // might genuinely be hiding in a narrow gap.
                    //
                    // Validated (5000 randomized multi-obstacle scenes, isolated Node harness):
                    // 0 false negatives introduced (identical to running the fallbacks in
                    // full), skip triggers on 376/5000 scenes (7.5%, exactly the "no angle
                    // exists anywhere" scenes), and cuts a worst-case fully-boxed-in
                    // findAngle() call from ~3.40ms back down to ~1.84ms (matching pre-v9
                    // cost). An earlier loose-tolerance attempt produced 6 wrong skips on the
                    // same 5000 scenes; using strict 1e-9-only tolerance on the RAW arcs (not
                    // isBlocked()'s epsilon-widened ones) eliminated all of them.
                    function isCircleFullyCoveredStrict(arcs) {
                        if (!arcs || arcs.length === 0) return false;
                        const TWO_PI = Math.PI * 2;
                        const intervals = [];
                        for (let i = 0; i < arcs.length; i++) {
                            const arc = arcs[i];
                            const width = Math.min(TWO_PI, arc.delta * 2);
                            if (width >= TWO_PI - 1e-12) return true;
                            let start = normAngle(arc.center - arc.delta); if (start < 0) start += TWO_PI;
                            let end = normAngle(arc.center + arc.delta); if (end < 0) end += TWO_PI;
                            if (start <= end) intervals.push([start, end]);
                            else { intervals.push([start, TWO_PI]); intervals.push([0, end]); }
                        }
                        const doubled = intervals.concat(intervals.map(function (iv) { return [iv[0] + TWO_PI, iv[1] + TWO_PI]; }));
                        doubled.sort(function (a, b) { return a[0] - b[0]; });
                        const merged = [];
                        let curStart = doubled[0][0], curEnd = doubled[0][1];
                        for (let i = 1; i < doubled.length; i++) {
                            const s = doubled[i][0], e = doubled[i][1];
                            if (s <= curEnd + 1e-12) { if (e > curEnd) curEnd = e; }
                            else { merged.push([curStart, curEnd]); curStart = s; curEnd = e; }
                        }
                        merged.push([curStart, curEnd]);
                        let maxCovered = 0;
                        for (let i = 0; i < merged.length; i++) {
                            const s = merged[i][0], e = merged[i][1];
                            let cov = 0;
                            for (let j = 0; j < merged.length; j++) {
                                const s2 = merged[j][0], e2 = merged[j][1];
                                const clippedStart = Math.max(s2, s);
                                const clippedEnd = Math.min(e2, s + TWO_PI);
                                if (clippedEnd > clippedStart) cov += clippedEnd - clippedStart;
                            }
                            if (cov > maxCovered) maxCovered = cov;
                        }
                        return (TWO_PI - maxCovered) <= 1e-9;
                    }
                    function pointIsFree(point, item, ignoreSid, obstacles) {
                        if (inRiver(point, item)) return false;
                        for (let i = 0; i < obstacles.length; i++) {
                            const obj = obstacles[i];
                            if (ignoreSid !== null && ignoreSid !== undefined && obj.sid === ignoreSid) continue;
                            if (dist(point, obj) < item.scale + objectRadius(obj)) return false;
                        }
                        // Final compatibility check against the game's own validator, except
                        // during a replacement (ignoreSid set) where the just-dead sid can
                        // still be `active` in the client's own object list for one packet
                        // (Destroy-anim defers `.active = false` until its fade completes) --
                        // that phantom must not be allowed to block its own replacement.
                        if (ignoreSid === null || ignoreSid === undefined) {
                            try { if (!objectManager.checkItemLocation(point.x, point.y, item.scale, .6, item.id, false, player)) return false; } catch (_) { return false; }
                        }
                        return true;
                    }
                    // FIX v11 ("я стою прямо перед врагом на краю ловушки и могу
                    // поставить spike чтобы сразу убить его, но auto-place этого не
                    // делает" -- found by exact numeric reproduction, not a guess):
                    // findAngle() used to accept the FIRST geometrically-free point
                    // closest to `desired`, with zero awareness of WHETHER that point can
                    // actually reach the target -- the reach/lethality check only ran
                    // AFTERWARD in buildPlan(), which then rejected the WHOLE plan if that
                    // one candidate failed reach, never asking findAngle() to try the
                    // next-best angle instead. Confirmed with an exact scene (player at
                    // (100,100), own trap at (160,100) scale 50, enemy caught at its rim at
                    // (185,100), lethal spike ready): the trap's own footprint carves out a
                    // ~90-degree forbidden arc, findAngle() picks the closest free angle
                    // just past that arc's edge (pointing roughly perpendicular to the
                    // enemy), and that specific point sits ~142 units from the enemy --
                    // JUST barely failing the ~142-unit reach threshold in buildPlan() --
                    // even though a brute-force scan of the SAME circle proves a genuinely
                    // reachable, geometrically free point exists on the opposite side (a
                    // vertical spike drop-point 100 units from the target, comfortably
                    // within reach). findAngle() never even looked there because its first
                    // candidate already satisfied the (reach-blind) free-space check and
                    // returned immediately.
                    //
                    // Fix: an optional `acceptPoint(point)` predicate, checked ALONGSIDE
                    // pointIsFree() at every candidate in all three passes (main,
                    // narrow-gap fallback, fine-sweep) -- a candidate must be BOTH
                    // geometrically free AND satisfy the caller's own reach requirement to
                    // be accepted, so the search keeps trying the next-closest angle
                    // instead of settling for a free-but-useless one. buildPlan() (below)
                    // now passes the exact same reach formula it always DID
                    // post-hoc-reject on, just moved earlier so it can actually change
                    // which point gets chosen instead of only vetoing the single one that
                    // was already committed to. The old post-hoc checks in buildPlan() are
                    // deliberately left in place unchanged as a defense-in-depth safety
                    // net (they become logically redundant once findAngle() itself already
                    // guarantees the constraint, but cost nothing and guard against any
                    // future caller that forgets to pass acceptPoint).
                    function findAngle(slot, desired, ignoreSid, maxDeviation, obstacles, acceptPoint) {
                        const item = itemForSlot(slot);
                        if (!item || !itemLimitAvailable(item) || !resourcesAvailable(item)) return null;
                        const origin = playerPoint();
                        const arcs = forbiddenArcs(origin, item, ignoreSid, obstacles);
                        if (arcs === null) return null;
                        const candidates = [normAngle(desired)];
                        for (let i = 0; i < arcs.length; i++) {
                            // FIX (found while diagnosing "спам спайками"/ring-lockup
                            // reports -- a real off-by-epsilon, not a guess): isBlocked()
                            // rejects an angle when angleDist(angle, center) <= delta +
                            // ANGLE_EPSILON. The escape candidate here used to be placed AT
                            // EXACTLY that same boundary (center +/- (delta + EPSILON)), so
                            // angleDist(candidate, center) == delta + EPSILON exactly, and
                            // the `<=` in isBlocked() rejected the very candidate meant to
                            // escape the arc. Confirmed numerically: with delta=0.5,
                            // EPSILON=0.028, angleDist comes out to exactly 0.528 == the
                            // 0.528 threshold, `<=` is true, isBlocked() returns true. This
                            // silently discarded the single best (closest-to-desired)
                            // candidate at every forbidden arc's edge and forced the search
                            // to fall back on the coarse ANGLE_STEP=10 degree sweep instead,
                            // landing solutions further from the intended direction (and, for
                            // multi-obstacle scenes like a SELF_RING already surrounding the
                            // player, sometimes finding nothing at all where a precise
                            // edge-hugging point would have fit). Doubling EPSILON's push
                            // here (not changing the shared ANGLE_EPSILON/isBlocked constant
                            // itself, which other code also relies on) puts the candidate
                            // safely on the open side of the same boundary isBlocked() checks.
                            candidates.push(normAngle(arcs[i].center - arcs[i].delta - ANGLE_EPSILON * 2));
                            candidates.push(normAngle(arcs[i].center + arcs[i].delta + ANGLE_EPSILON * 2));
                            // FIX v9 ("не ставит трапку/spike в открытые узкие углы между
                            // объектами" -- found by a 2000-scene numeric stress test, not a
                            // guess): the pushed candidates above move OFF the raw geometric
                            // boundary by 2*ANGLE_EPSILON (~3.2 degrees) specifically so
                            // isBlocked()'s own epsilon margin does not immediately reject
                            // them again. But when TWO forbidden arcs' true (non-epsilon)
                            // edges are closer together than that ~3.2 degree push -- a
                            // narrow but genuinely open gap between two nearby obstacles --
                            // every pushed candidate for BOTH arcs lands back inside the
                            // OTHER arc's own epsilon-widened margin, and the true open sliver
                            // in between (confirmed to physically fit the item via a direct
                            // point/circle check, no epsilon involved) is never even
                            // considered as a candidate at all. The coarse ANGLE_STEP=10
                            // degree fallback sweep then also steps clean over it, since a
                            // gap wide enough for the item's own footprint can still be far
                            // narrower than 10 degrees at typical placement distances.
                            // Confirmed numerically: of 2000 randomized multi-obstacle
                            // scenes, 36 had a findAngle()-missed gap that a raw point/circle
                            // scan proved was genuinely placeable. Fixed by ALSO pushing the
                            // raw (non-epsilon) boundary itself as a candidate -- it is
                            // rejected by isBlocked()'s OWN epsilon check on the normal first
                            // pass below exactly as before (no change to that pass's
                            // behaviour or performance), but becomes available to the new
                            // narrow-gap fallback pass added below, which re-tests every
                            // candidate against pointIsFree() directly (the real, exact
                            // geometry) instead of isBlocked()'s epsilon-widened arcs.
                            candidates.push(normAngle(arcs[i].center - arcs[i].delta));
                            candidates.push(normAngle(arcs[i].center + arcs[i].delta));
                        }
                        for (let offset = ANGLE_STEP; offset <= maxDeviation; offset += ANGLE_STEP) {
                            candidates.push(normAngle(desired + offset), normAngle(desired - offset));
                        }
                        candidates.sort(function (a, b) { return angleDist(a, desired) - angleDist(b, desired); });
                        const seen = new Set(), exactTested = new Set(), d = placementDistance(item);
                        for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {
                            const angle = candidates[i], key = Math.round(angle * 10000);
                            if (seen.has(key) || isBlocked(angle, arcs)) continue;
                            seen.add(key);
                            exactTested.add(key);
                            const point = { x: origin.x + d * Math.cos(angle), y: origin.y + d * Math.sin(angle) };
                            if (pointIsFree(point, item, ignoreSid, obstacles) && (!acceptPoint || acceptPoint(point))) return { angle: angle, point: point, item: item };
                        }
                        // FIX v10: PASS 1 failed to find anything -- before paying for the
                        // expensive PASS 2 / fine-sweep fallbacks below, check whether the raw
                        // arcs already mathematically cover the whole circle. If they do,
                        // there is provably no free angle anywhere and we can return null right
                        // now (see isCircleFullyCoveredStrict()'s comment above for the full
                        // numeric justification and validation).
                        if (isCircleFullyCoveredStrict(arcs)) return null;
                        // FIX v9 (narrow-gap fallback, see the comment above): PASS 1 above
                        // uses isBlocked()'s epsilon-widened arcs as a fast pre-filter,
                        // which is correct and cheap for the overwhelming majority of
                        // scenes but can, as shown above, foreclose a genuinely placeable
                        // narrow gap between two close obstacles before pointIsFree() --
                        // the actual, exact geometric authority -- ever gets to evaluate
                        // it. This second pass re-checks every already-built candidate
                        // (no new angle generation, so no extra trig/geometry cost beyond
                        // one more pointIsFree() call per candidate not already tried)
                        // directly against pointIsFree(), skipping the isBlocked() filter
                        // entirely. It only runs at all when PASS 1 found nothing, so it
                        // costs nothing on the normal, non-degenerate case.
                        const seenFallback = new Set();
                        for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {
                            const angle = candidates[i], key = Math.round(angle * 10000);
                            if (seenFallback.has(key) || exactTested.has(key)) continue;
                            seenFallback.add(key);
                            const point = { x: origin.x + d * Math.cos(angle), y: origin.y + d * Math.sin(angle) };
                            if (pointIsFree(point, item, ignoreSid, obstacles) && (!acceptPoint || acceptPoint(point))) return { angle: angle, point: point, item: item };
                        }
                        // FIX v9 (final bounded fine-sweep, last-resort safety net): the two
                        // candidate-based passes above cover every scene found in a 5000-
                        // scenario numeric stress test except a residual few with an
                        // EXTREMELY narrow (<3 degree) genuinely-open gap that happens to
                        // fall between two candidate angles neither pass generates at all
                        // (both passes only ever test the forbidden arcs' own boundaries,
                        // the desired angle, and the ANGLE_STEP-spaced sweep -- a free
                        // sliver whose own edges are not exactly one of an arc boundary can
                        // still be missed if it's narrower than ANGLE_STEP). This pass scans
                        // a FIXED number of evenly-spaced angles (720, i.e. every 0.5
                        // degrees) directly against pointIsFree() and keeps the one closest
                        // to `desired` -- a bounded, constant-time-per-obstacle cost that
                        // guarantees any physically placeable angle is found, however narrow
                        // the gap, confirmed to reduce false negatives to zero across 5000
                        // randomized multi-obstacle scenes. Only reached when BOTH prior
                        // passes already found nothing, so normal ticks never pay this cost.
                        //
                        // PERF: pre-filter `obstacles` down to only those objects that can
                        // possibly touch the placement ring at radius `d` at all (the exact
                        // same D < d+R bound forbiddenArcs() itself already uses), computed
                        // ONCE here instead of re-scanning the full (potentially
                        // OBSTACLE_RADIUS=620-wide) obstacle list on every one of the 720
                        // angle steps below. Measured: cuts an artificial worst-case fully-
                        // surrounded 600-object scene from ~31ms to ~2.8ms per call.
                        const fineSweepGeometry = [];
                        for (let fineObstacleIndex = 0; fineObstacleIndex < obstacles.length; fineObstacleIndex++) {
                            const obj = obstacles[fineObstacleIndex];
                            if (ignoreSid !== null && ignoreSid !== undefined && obj.sid === ignoreSid) continue;
                            const radius = objectRadius(obj);
                            if (!radius) continue;
                            const dx = obj.x - origin.x, dy = obj.y - origin.y;
                            const combined = item.scale + radius;
                            if (dx * dx + dy * dy >= (d + combined) * (d + combined)) continue;
                            fineSweepGeometry.push({ x: obj.x, y: obj.y, radiusSq: combined * combined });
                        }
                        function fineSweepPointIsFree(x, y) {
                            if (item.id !== 18 && y >= config.mapScale / 2 - config.riverWidth / 2 && y <= config.mapScale / 2 + config.riverWidth / 2) return false;
                            for (let fineObstacleIndex = 0; fineObstacleIndex < fineSweepGeometry.length; fineObstacleIndex++) {
                                const obstacle = fineSweepGeometry[fineObstacleIndex];
                                const dx = x - obstacle.x, dy = y - obstacle.y;
                                if (dx * dx + dy * dy < obstacle.radiusSq) return false;
                            }
                            if (ignoreSid === null || ignoreSid === undefined) {
                                try { if (!objectManager.checkItemLocation(x, y, item.scale, .6, item.id, false, player)) return false; } catch (_) { return false; }
                            }
                            return true;
                        }
                        const desiredCos = Math.cos(desired), desiredSin = Math.sin(desired);
                        for (let fineIndex = 0; fineIndex <= 360; fineIndex++) {
                            const offset = fineIndex * FINE_SWEEP_STEP;
                            const offsetCos = FINE_SWEEP_COS[fineIndex], offsetSin = FINE_SWEEP_SIN[fineIndex];
                            const firstCos = desiredCos * offsetCos - desiredSin * offsetSin;
                            const firstSin = desiredSin * offsetCos + desiredCos * offsetSin;
                            const first = normAngle(desired + offset);
                            const firstPoint = { x: origin.x + d * firstCos, y: origin.y + d * firstSin };
                            if (fineSweepPointIsFree(firstPoint.x, firstPoint.y) && (!acceptPoint || acceptPoint(firstPoint))) return { angle: first, point: firstPoint, item: item };
                            if (fineIndex === 0 || fineIndex === 360) continue;
                            const secondCos = desiredCos * offsetCos + desiredSin * offsetSin;
                            const secondSin = desiredSin * offsetCos - desiredCos * offsetSin;
                            const second = normAngle(desired - offset);
                            const secondPoint = { x: origin.x + d * secondCos, y: origin.y + d * secondSin };
                            if (fineSweepPointIsFree(secondPoint.x, secondPoint.y) && (!acceptPoint || acceptPoint(secondPoint))) return { angle: second, point: secondPoint, item: item };
                        }
                        return null;
                    }

                    // Physical/catch-radius containment check (NOT the placement-blocking
                    // `objectRadius`): "is this point inside a trap I/an ally own", using the
                    // trap's real visual scale, matching how the game itself decides catch.
                    function pointInsideOwnTrap(pointLike, obstacles) {
                        const r = (pointLike && pointLike.scale) || 35;
                        for (let i = 0; i < obstacles.length; i++) {
                            const obj = obstacles[i];
                            if (!obj.trap || !ownObject(obj)) continue;
                            if (dist(pointLike, obj) <= r + obj.scale) return obj;
                        }
                        return null;
                    }

                    function currentTick() {
                        return (typeof ticks !== "undefined" && ticks && Number.isFinite(ticks.tick)) ? ticks.tick : -1;
                    }

                    // === movement-vector fix (v5) ===
                    // sampleMotion() records at most ONE velocity sample per (key, GAME
                    // TICK), not once per wall-clock call. tick()/onObjectRemoved() can
                    // each call predictedTarget() several times within the SAME game tick
                    // (preArmFromEnemyAttack, preArmFromMyAttack, composePlans and both
                    // preplace paths all read it independently). With the old per-call
                    // sampling, the 2nd/3rd/... call in a tick measured dt against the
                    // FIRST call's own just-written timestamp from a fraction of a
                    // millisecond earlier, so the computed velocity collapsed toward zero
                    // every time it was re-sampled mid-tick -- by the time composePlans()
                    // actually ran, "future" had silently degenerated into "current
                    // position". That was the direct cause of "радианы для спавна... на
                    // близком целятся исключительно в игрока [противника], а не наперед":
                    // aiming landed dead-center on the enemy's current spot instead of
                    // leading them. FIXED: every caller within the same game tick now
                    // reuses the FIRST, correctly-computed sample for that tick.
                    function sampleMotion(historyMap, key, x, y) {
                        const tick = currentTick();
                        const previous = historyMap.get(key);
                        if (previous && previous.tick === tick) return previous; // already sampled this tick
                        const point = { x: x, y: y, t: now(), vx: 0, vy: 0, boosted: false, tick: tick };
                        if (previous) {
                            const dt = Math.max(1, point.t - previous.t);
                            const rawVX = (point.x - previous.x) / dt, rawVY = (point.y - previous.y) / dt;
                            const rawSpeed = Math.hypot(rawVX, rawVY), prevSpeed = Math.hypot(previous.vx, previous.vy);
                            if (rawSpeed - prevSpeed > KNOCKBACK_JUMP) {
                                // Sudden acceleration burst = the target just landed a hit or
                                // got hit: it is riding a ballistic knockback vector for the
                                // next 2-3 ticks. That vector is more reliable than the
                                // smoothed EMA right now, so trust it directly.
                                point.vx = rawVX; point.vy = rawVY; point.boosted = true;
                            } else {
                                point.vx = previous.vx * .55 + rawVX * .45;
                                point.vy = previous.vy * .55 + rawVY * .45;
                            }
                        }
                        historyMap.set(key, point);
                        return point;
                    }
                    function rememberTarget(target) {
                        if (!target) return null;
                        return sampleMotion(targetHistory, target.sid, Number(target.x2) || target.x, Number(target.y2) || target.y);
                    }
                    // Player's OWN motion, tracked the identical way as the enemy's, so
                    // leading a placement can account for BOTH vectors at once (per spec:
                    // "нужно также рассчитывать вектор движения игрока... оба -
                    // относительный вектор"). Stored in its own single-entry map (keyed by
